PR surface: Source +1528, Tests +2543, Docs +21, Other -2. Total +4090 across 58 files.

target.body:
Related: #95750
Follow-up: #105877

## Current Handoff Status

This PR is paused for handoff. No partial rebase or SDK follow-up change has been pushed.

- PR head remains **5d7c3d78e54e328aa5448ba2b1a4a8fdc49a1078** on **feat/issue-95750**.
- The maintainer worktree is clean on **feature/pr-96230-recovery-fuse** at that exact head.
- The last fetched development target was **upstream/main@a03df5fd5898e24facd38c07d9d9e60a047f0111**.
- GitHub currently reports the PR as **CONFLICTING / DIRTY**.
- A latest-main rebase was started only to enumerate conflicts, then deliberately aborted. The PR branch contains none of those partial resolutions.
- The prior exact merge result and CI below remain valid proof for the recorded old merge base, but they are not current-main landability proof.
- A handoff audit found one remaining Plugin SDK runtime gap in the deprecated whole-store compatibility APIs. The modern row-level SDK APIs are contained, but the PR must not merge until the legacy gap described below is fixed and tested.

Local-only recovery points in the existing workspace:

~~~text
backup/pr-96230-pre-a03-rebase
  5d7c3d78e54e328aa5448ba2b1a4a8fdc49a1078

temp/pr-96230-squashed-rebase
  11d4b0252b6f287d361cbad0c849ded9c1a23f87
~~~

The temporary branch is a single final-tree squash whose parent is the fixed development baseline. It was created because replaying 48 iterative commits starts with obsolete flat-field designs that the final state machine already replaced. It is local only and was not pushed.

### Remaining work, in order

1. Rebase the final PR effect onto the then-current **upstream/main**. Prefer replaying the final reviewed tree rather than reviving obsolete intermediate recovery designs.
2. Resolve the current-main conflicts using the notes below.
3. Close the deprecated Plugin SDK **loadSessionStore/updateSessionStore** runtime boundary gap and add focused regression tests.
4. Generate and semantically inspect the Plugin SDK surface. Recovery internals must not appear, and a checksum-only baseline update must not be used to hide a semantic change.
5. Run focused recovery, SDK, compaction, Doctor, and Gateway admission tests through the configured Crabbox provider.
6. Run changed lanes, targeted format/lint, extension contract checks, Plugin SDK surface/baseline checks, and full build as selected by the rebased diff.
7. Run one final default-Codex Auto Review and address every accepted/actionable finding.
8. Push the new head to the original author branch **feat/issue-95750**, refresh this status and evidence, then verify exact-head and exact-merge-result CI.

### Latest-main conflict inventory

The aborted rebase against **a03df5fd5898e24facd38c07d9d9e60a047f0111** found conflicts in:

- **docs/gateway/restart-recovery.md**
- **packages/gateway-client/src/client.ts**
- **packages/gateway-client/src/client.watchdog.test.ts**
- **src/agents/agent-command.ts**
- **src/agents/main-session-restart-recovery.ts**
- **src/agents/main-session-restart-recovery.test.ts**
- **src/gateway/server-methods/agent.ts**

Resolution notes:

- Documentation must retain current main's durable Control UI dispatch/idempotency description and add this PR's separate cross-boot charged-attempt fuse.
- Current main moved request sending into **GatewayProtocolClient/GatewayProtocolRequests**. Preserve that owner. Adapt **onDispatched** into **packages/gateway-client/src/protocol-client-types.ts** and **packages/gateway-client/src/protocol-requests.ts**, invoking it only after **socket.send** succeeds and routing callback failures through the existing callback-error path. Do not resurrect the removed pending-request implementation in **client.ts**.
- In **agent-command.ts**, retain current main's **trackedRestartRecoveryDeliveryClaim** and claim-cleanup helper while preserving this PR's WeakMap-based internal recovery candidate and foreground owner lease.
- In **server-methods/agent.ts**, retain both current main's **ExpectedExistingSessionChangedError** response path and this PR's recovery reservation/admission conflict response.
- In **main-session-restart-recovery.ts**, preserve current main's Control UI admission and durable idempotency work. Integrate the final recovery state/store owner; do not choose either conflicted whole file wholesale.
- Preserve pending-final and compaction-failure delivery behavior from current main together with this PR's recovery cleanup and generation fences.

## What Problem This Solves

A Gateway restart could repeatedly select the same interrupted main session for automatic recovery. The existing retry loop was process-local, so supervisor backoff only delayed the next attempt: a session that never became healthy could be dispatched again after every restart without a durable ceiling.

This PR adds a durable, session-owned recovery fuse. The first three accepted or acceptance-uncertain automatic recovery attempts may dispatch. Before a fourth dispatch, OpenClaw tombstones the session and requires operator or user recovery through inspection and **/new** or reset.

## Why This Change Was Made

### Final Recovery Architecture

#### Internal state and policy owner

The durable state is one core-internal aggregate: **InternalSessionEntry.mainRestartRecovery**. It is deliberately separate from the public **SessionEntry** contract.

The aggregate records:

- a recovery cycle and monotonic revision;
- **chargedAttempts**;
- an optional pre-dispatch reservation carrying run, attempt, and lifecycle-generation identity;
- lifecycle-generation-scoped foreground claim tokens; and
- an optional tombstone with its terminal reason.

**src/agents/main-session-recovery-state.ts** is the single pure transition owner. It defines interrupted-session observation, attempt preparation, exact reservation cancellation, admission, foreground claim/release, failure, tombstone, Doctor repair, and healthy/reset clearing.

The policy is:

- Persist the charge and reservation before dispatch.
- Roll the charge back only when the exact reserved request is known not to have been accepted.
- Keep the charge when dispatch acceptance is uncertain, including a stale reservation observed after process restart.
- Allow three charged attempts and commit the tombstone before any fourth dispatch or best-effort operator notice.
- Do not expire the main-session budget merely because time passes.
- Clear the aggregate after a non-aborted session-store settlement, session replacement, or reset.

**restartRecoveryRuns** remains a lifecycle-generation fence only; it does not double as the durable budget. Subagent orphan recovery also remains separate, retaining its existing two-attempt, two-minute rapid re-wedge policy.

#### Atomic persistence and admission

**src/agents/main-session-recovery-store.ts** is the persistence owner. Callers submit closed recovery commands instead of mutating fields. The store rereads the canonical SQLite row and applies identity, revision, reservation, and lifecycle-generation checks inside the synchronous session-store write transaction.

Gateway and direct agent-command ingress share the same ownership rules:

- a recovery attempt is reserved atomically before fallible dispatch work;
- final Gateway acceptance revalidates and admits the exact reservation;
- known pre-accept rejection cancels the exact reservation and restores the interrupted state;
- abort and foreground-owner races cannot leak a run registry or silently consume ownership;
- overlapping foreground admissions use token sets scoped to the lifecycle generation; and
- reservation cancellation follows its identity if a legacy session key is canonicalized during admission.

Tombstone state is durable before notification. Doctor reads and repairs through the same canonical session accessor and does not re-enable a tombstoned session. Cache identity uses nanosecond **ctime/mtime** plus size so same-size writes within one millisecond cannot hide recovery or Doctor updates.

The previously verified merge preserved then-current **main** pending-final delivery and compaction-failure behavior. A new rebase must re-prove that invariant against the latest main.

### Plugin SDK Boundary

Recovery coordination is an internal persistence concern, not a new plugin contract.

Implemented at the current PR head:

- Public **SessionEntry** keeps all previously shipped fields but excludes **mainRestartRecovery**; core persistence uses **InternalSessionEntry**.
- Modern **getSessionEntry/listSessionEntries** reads project the canonical row to the public shape at runtime.
- Modern **patchSessionEntry/updateSessionStoreEntry/upsertSessionEntry** strip runtime-escaped private input and preserve existing internal recovery state.
- The internal agent-command preparation path carries its recovery candidate out of band; the published testing result does not contain **recoveryCandidateEntry**.
- The generated SDK type surface contains no recovery-internal concept, and the PR does not update **docs/.generated/plugin-sdk-api-baseline.sha256**.

Remaining runtime gap:

- Deprecated **loadSessionStore** currently returns complete accessor rows without calling the public projection. A plugin can therefore observe **mainRestartRecovery** at runtime even though the public type omits it.
- Deprecated **updateSessionStore** currently passes a clone of the complete internal store to the plugin callback. The callback can observe the private field and can erase it by replacing an existing row with a public entry.
- Existing recovery-boundary tests cover only the modern row-level reads and mutations, so this compatibility path is unproved.

Required fix shape:

- Project every row before passing the compatibility store to plugin code.
- After the callback, reconcile only public rows/fields into the internal working store.
- Preserve the existing row's **mainRestartRecovery** across same-key public replacement/update.
- Strip runtime-escaped **mainRestartRecovery** from newly created or replaced public inputs.
- Preserve intentional row deletion semantics.
- Add tests that seed internal recovery state, prove **loadSessionStore** and the **updateSessionStore** callback cannot see it, update a public field, and prove the canonical internal state is unchanged.
- Add a type-escape injection test for compatibility-store creation/update.

The existing exported Plugin SDK testing surface must not be removed here because it is already part of the shipped SDK contract. The broader replacement of its wildcard/internal inference with an explicitly owned stable surface remains tracked in #105877.

### Non-goals

This PR does not:

- remove older shipped session fields such as **restartRecoveryRuns** or subagent recovery state;
- redesign the complete Plugin SDK session API;
- remove the shipped whole-store compatibility APIs before their documented deprecation window;
- change the Gateway wire protocol, provider routing, config, or environment surface;
- add JSON fallback, dual writes, or runtime compatibility shims; or
- change recovery budget, quarantine, or subagent product semantics beyond the main-session fuse described above.

## Design Evolution

The implementation converged through these stages:

1. **Persist the missing cross-boot budget.** The first version added flat retry/quarantine fields around the existing process-local loop. That established the core requirement but left policy spread across callers and did not fully model ownership races.
2. **Separate lifecycle suppression from retry accounting.** **restartRecoveryRuns** was considered as a compatibility floor, then kept strictly as a generation fence. Transcript preflight and other static, non-dispatched failures were separated from accepted or acceptance-uncertain dispatches so they do not consume the durable budget.
3. **Choose the main-session reset contract.** Reusing the subagent two-minute rapid-rewedge window was considered. It was rejected because supervisor backoff can space main-session retries minutes or hours apart without proving health. Main recovery therefore uses cumulative charged attempts until healthy settlement, while subagents keep their existing rapid-window policy.
4. **Move to one state machine and one atomic store owner.** Flat fields became the internal aggregate. Pure transitions and closed store commands added pre-dispatch reservations, exact rollback, lifecycle-generation fences, overlapping foreground tokens, ingress ownership, and canonical-key migration handling.
5. **Close canonical-owner paths.** Review and CI exposed gaps around Doctor JSON-versus-SQLite ownership, pending-final cleanup during compaction conflicts, and admission abort/rejection races. Doctor moved to the canonical accessor, and the verified merge preserved then-current main delivery semantics while keeping recovery invariants.
6. **Contain the modern Plugin SDK boundary.** Semantic API comparison showed that importing the internal persistence row and inferring the agent testing return could publish **mainRestartRecovery** and **recoveryCandidateEntry**. Public and internal session types were split, modern reads/writes gained runtime projection and preservation, and the internal candidate moved out of the published testing result.
7. **Handoff audit found the remaining compatibility seam.** Full entrypoint review showed that the deprecated whole-store **loadSessionStore/updateSessionStore** adapters still expose complete internal rows. This remains in scope because those APIs are shipped Plugin SDK contracts and whole-row writes can destroy the same recovery owner state this PR introduces.

Alternatives rejected:

- Process-local retry accounting: cannot survive the restart loop it is meant to stop.
- Deriving the durable budget from **restartRecoveryRuns**: conflates lifecycle fencing with product retry policy.
- Reusing the subagent rapid-time window: elapsed time and supervisor backoff do not demonstrate main-session health.
- Exposing the internal persistence row through any SDK entrypoint: turns recovery ownership into a public compatibility burden and lets whole-row writes destroy private state.
- Removing the deprecated compatibility or testing exports here: would break shipped SDK surfaces and exceed the recovery-specific scope.
- Replaying all 48 iterative commits onto new main without consolidation: repeatedly resurrects obsolete intermediate architectures and makes conflict resolution less reliable than applying the final reviewed tree.

## User Impact

A wedged main session can no longer trigger unbounded automatic resume across Gateway restarts. After three charged accepted or acceptance-uncertain attempts, OpenClaw quarantines the session before another automatic dispatch and asks the operator to inspect it and use **/new** or reset.

Healthy progress, replacement, or reset restores the full budget. Waiting alone does not. Existing plugin-visible session fields must remain available, while plugins must neither see nor accidentally overwrite the internal recovery state. The modern APIs satisfy that requirement at the current head; the deprecated whole-store compatibility APIs still require the fix documented above.

## Evidence

Previously reviewed range:

~~~text
base: 08843c74de0f632ef5b7808a9fcf9cb6c85ac967
head: 5d7c3d78e54e328aa5448ba2b1a4a8fdc49a1078
~~~

The previously verified merge result was **b0a38e374dcb5cb7566976560ad7182b49c81f49**, merging this head into **main@ffff72c43aedf5bdeb32a6836f577850207f8573**.

Proof valid for that exact old merge result:

- Focused recovery, compaction, and session proof: 230 tests passed on Docker Crabbox lease **cbx_c3e4e0c8917b**.
- Targeted lint and full **pnpm build** passed on Docker Crabbox lease **cbx_3a3579299845** (actual provider **local-container**, Docker runtime).
- Exact-head GitHub CI: all 15 workflows passed. The CI workflow completed with 50 successful jobs, 11 conditionally skipped jobs, and no failures: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29235146885
- The generated SDK type surface excluded **mainRestartRecovery** and **recoveryCandidateEntry**, with no recovery-internal checksum-only baseline update.
- Final default-Codex Auto Review completed with every accepted/actionable finding addressed for that head.
- Final ClawSweeper review found no contributor-facing blocker for that head.
- Real Telegram Desktop scenario proof remains available:
  - workflow: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28780448010
  - artifact: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28780448010/artifacts/8106022765
  - manifest: https://artifacts.openclaw.ai/mantis/telegram-desktop/pr-96230/run-28780448010-1/index.json

The Telegram baseline replayed the exhausted recovery turn before handling a fresh message. The candidate tombstoned the exhausted row and handled the fresh Telegram message without another automatic resume.

Current proof gaps:

- Deprecated **loadSessionStore/updateSessionStore** runtime projection and internal-state preservation are not implemented or tested.
- The PR is not rebased onto latest main and currently conflicts.
- No focused, changed-lane, build, Auto Review, exact-head CI, or exact-merge-result CI exists for the future rebased/fixed head.

target.body:
Related: #95750
Follow-up: #105877

## Current Handoff Status

This PR is paused for handoff. No partial rebase or SDK follow-up change has been pushed.

- PR head remains **5d7c3d78e54e328aa5448ba2b1a4a8fdc49a1078** on **feat/issue-95750**.
- The maintainer worktree is clean on **feature/pr-96230-recovery-fuse** at that exact head.
- The last fetched development target was **upstream/main@a03df5fd5898e24facd38c07d9d9e60a047f0111**.
- GitHub currently reports the PR as **CONFLICTING / DIRTY**.
- A latest-main rebase was started only to enumerate conflicts, then deliberately aborted. The PR branch contains none of those partial resolutions.
- The prior exact merge result and CI below remain valid proof for the recorded old merge base, but they are not current-main landability proof.
- A handoff audit found one remaining Plugin SDK runtime gap in the deprecated whole-store compatibility APIs. The modern row-level SDK APIs are contained, but the PR must not merge until the legacy gap described below is fixed and tested.

Local-only recovery points in the existing workspace:

~~~text
backup/pr-96230-pre-a03-rebase
  5d7c3d78e54e328aa5448ba2b1a4a8fdc49a1078

temp/pr-96230-squashed-rebase
  11d4b0252b6f287d361cbad0c849ded9c1a23f87
~~~

The temporary branch is a single final-tree squash whose parent is the fixed development baseline. It was created because replaying 48 iterative commits starts with obsolete flat-field designs that the final state machine already replaced. It is local only and was not pushed.

### Remaining work, in order

1. Rebase the final PR effect onto the then-current **upstream/main**. Prefer replaying the final reviewed tree rather than reviving obsolete intermediate recovery designs.
2. Resolve the current-main conflicts using the notes below.
3. Close the deprecated Plugin SDK **loadSessionStore/updateSessionStore** runtime boundary gap and add focused regression tests.
4. Generate and semantically inspect the Plugin SDK surface. Recovery internals must not appear, and a checksum-only baseline update must not be used to hide a semantic change.
5. Run focused recovery, SDK, compaction, Doctor, and Gateway admission tests through the configured Crabbox provider.
6. Run changed lanes, targeted format/lint, extension contract checks, Plugin SDK surface/baseline checks, and full build as selected by the rebased diff.
7. Run one final default-Codex Auto Review and address every accepted/actionable finding.
8. Push the new head to the original author branch **feat/issue-95750**, refresh this status and evidence, then verify exact-head and exact-merge-result CI.

### Latest-main conflict inventory

The aborted rebase against **a03df5fd5898e24facd38c07d9d9e60a047f0111** found conflicts in:

- **docs/gateway/restart-recovery.md**
- **packages/gateway-client/src/client.ts**
- **packages/gateway-client/src/client.watchdog.test.ts**
- **src/agents/agent-command.ts**
- **src/agents/main-session-restart-recovery.ts**
- **src/agents/main-session-restart-recovery.test.ts**
- **src/gateway/server-methods/agent.ts**

Resolution notes:

- Documentation must retain current main's durable Control UI dispatch/idempotency description and add this PR's separate cross-boot charged-attempt fuse.
- Current main moved request sending into **GatewayProtocolClient/GatewayProtocolRequests**. Preserve that owner. Adapt **onDispatched** into **packages/gateway-client/src/protocol-client-types.ts** and **packages/gateway-client/src/protocol-requests.ts**, invoking it only after **socket.send** succeeds and routing callback failures through the existing callback-error path. Do not resurrect the removed pending-request implementation in **client.ts**.
- In **agent-command.ts**, retain current main's **trackedRestartRecoveryDeliveryClaim** and claim-cleanup helper while preserving this PR's WeakMap-based internal recovery candidate and foreground owner lease.
- In **server-methods/agent.ts**, retain both current main's **ExpectedExistingSessionChangedError** response path and this PR's recovery reservation/admission conflict response.
- In **main-session-restart-recovery.ts**, preserve current main's Control UI admission and durable idempotency work. Integrate the final recovery state/store owner; do not choose either conflicted whole file wholesale.
- Preserve pending-final and compaction-failure delivery behavior from current main together with this PR's recovery cleanup and generation fences.

## What Problem This Solves

A Gateway restart could repeatedly select the same interrupted main session for automatic recovery. The existing retry loop was process-local, so supervisor backoff only delayed the next attempt: a session that never became healthy could be dispatched again after every restart without a durable ceiling.

This PR adds a durable, session-owned recovery fuse. The first three accepted or acceptance-uncertain automatic recovery attempts may dispatch. Before a fourth dispatch, OpenClaw tombstones the session and requires operator or user recovery through inspection and **/new** or reset.

## Why This Change Was Made

### Final Recovery Architecture

#### Internal state and policy owner

The durable state is one core-internal aggregate: **InternalSessionEntry.mainRestartRecovery**. It is deliberately separate from the public **SessionEntry** contract.

The aggregate records:

- a recovery cycle and monotonic revision;
- **chargedAttempts**;
- an optional pre-dispatch reservation carrying run, attempt, and lifecycle-generation identity;
- lifecycle-generation-scoped foreground claim tokens; and
- an optional tombstone with its terminal reason.

**src/agents/main-session-recovery-state.ts** is the single pure transition owner. It defines interrupted-session observation, attempt preparation, exact reservation cancellation, admission, foreground claim/release, failure, tombstone, Doctor repair, and healthy/reset clearing.

The policy is:

- Persist the charge and reservation before dispatch.
- Roll the charge back only when the exact reserved request is known not to have been accepted.
- Keep the charge when dispatch acceptance is uncertain, including a stale reservation observed after process restart.
- Allow three charged attempts and commit the tombstone before any fourth dispatch or best-effort operator notice.
- Do not expire the main-session budget merely because time passes.
- Clear the aggregate after a non-aborted session-store settlement, session replacement, or reset.

**restartRecoveryRuns** remains a lifecycle-generation fence only; it does not double as the durable budget. Subagent orphan recovery also remains separate, retaining its existing two-attempt, two-minute rapid re-wedge policy.

#### Atomic persistence and admission

**src/agents/main-session-recovery-store.ts** is the persistence owner. Callers submit closed recovery commands instead of mutating fields. The store rereads the canonical SQLite row and applies identity, revision, reservation, and lifecycle-generation checks inside the synchronous session-store write transaction.

Gateway and direct agent-command ingress share the same ownership rules:

- a recovery attempt is reserved atomically before fallible dispatch work;
- final Gateway acceptance revalidates and admits the exact reservation;
- known pre-accept rejection cancels the exact reservation and restores the interrupted state;
- abort and foreground-owner races cannot leak a run registry or silently consume ownership;
- overlapping foreground admissions use token sets scoped to the lifecycle generation; and
- reservation cancellation follows its identity if a legacy session key is canonicalized during admission.

Tombstone state is durable before notification. Doctor reads and repairs through the same canonical session accessor and does not re-enable a tombstoned session. Cache identity uses nanosecond **ctime/mtime** plus size so same-size writes within one millisecond cannot hide recovery or Doctor updates.

The previously verified merge preserved then-current **main** pending-final delivery and compaction-failure behavior. A new rebase must re-prove that invariant against the latest main.

### Plugin SDK Boundary

Recovery coordination is an internal persistence concern, not a new plugin contract.

Implemented at the current PR head:

- Public **SessionEntry** keeps all previously shipped fields but excludes **mainRestartRecovery**; core persistence uses **InternalSessionEntry**.
- Modern **getSessionEntry/listSessionEntries** reads project the canonical row to the public shape at runtime.
- Modern **patchSessionEntry/updateSessionStoreEntry/upsertSessionEntry** strip runtime-escaped private input and preserve existing internal recovery state.
- The internal agent-command preparation path carries its recovery candidate out of band; the published testing result does not contain **recoveryCandidateEntry**.
- The generated SDK type surface contains no recovery-internal concept, and the PR does not update **docs/.generated/plugin-sdk-api-baseline.sha256**.

Remaining runtime gap:

- Deprecated **loadSessionStore** currently returns complete accessor rows without calling the public projection. A plugin can therefore observe **mainRestartRecovery** at runtime even though the public type omits it.
- Deprecated **updateSessionStore** currently passes a clone of the complete internal store to the plugin callback. The callback can observe the private field and can erase it by replacing an existing row with a public entry.
- Existing recovery-boundary tests cover only the modern row-level reads and mutations, so this compatibility path is unproved.

Required fix shape:

- Project every row before passing the compatibility store to plugin code.
- After the callback, reconcile only public rows/fields into the internal working store.
- Preserve the existing row's **mainRestartRecovery** across same-key public replacement/update.
- Strip runtime-escaped **mainRestartRecovery** from newly created or replaced public inputs.
- Preserve intentional row deletion semantics.
- Add tests that seed internal recovery state, prove **loadSessionStore** and the **updateSessionStore** callback cannot see it, update a public field, and prove the canonical internal state is unchanged.
- Add a type-escape injection test for compatibility-store creation/update.

The existing exported Plugin SDK testing surface must not be removed here because it is already part of the shipped SDK contract. The broader replacement of its wildcard/internal inference with an explicitly owned stable surface remains tracked in #105877.

### Non-goals

This PR does not:

- remove older shipped session fields such as **restartRecoveryRuns** or subagent recovery state;
- redesign the complete Plugin SDK session API;
- remove the shipped whole-store compatibility APIs before their documented deprecation window;
- change the Gateway wire protocol, provider routing, config, or environment surface;
- add JSON fallback, dual writes, or runtime compatibility shims; or
- change recovery budget, quarantine, or subagent product semantics beyond the main-session fuse described above.

## Design Evolution

The implementation converged through these stages:

1. **Persist the missing cross-boot budget.** The first version added flat retry/quarantine fields around the existing process-local loop. That established the core requirement but left policy spread across callers and did not fully model ownership races.
2. **Separate lifecycle suppression from retry accounting.** **restartRecoveryRuns** was considered as a compatibility floor, then kept strictly as a generation fence. Transcript preflight and other static, non-dispatched failures were separated from accepted or acceptance-uncertain dispatches so they do not consume the durable budget.
3. **Choose the main-session reset contract.** Reusing the subagent two-minute rapid-rewedge window was considered. It was rejected because supervisor backoff can space main-session retries minutes or hours apart without proving health. Main recovery therefore uses cumulative charged attempts until healthy settlement, while subagents keep their existing rapid-window policy.
4. **Move to one state machine and one atomic store owner.** Flat fields became the internal aggregate. Pure transitions and closed store commands added pre-dispatch reservations, exact rollback, lifecycle-generation fences, overlapping foreground tokens, ingress ownership, and canonical-key migration handling.
5. **Close canonical-owner paths.** Review and CI exposed gaps around Doctor JSON-versus-SQLite ownership, pending-final cleanup during compaction conflicts, and admission abort/rejection races. Doctor moved to the canonical accessor, and the verified merge preserved then-current main delivery semantics while keeping recovery invariants.
6. **Contain the modern Plugin SDK boundary.** Semantic API comparison showed that importing the internal persistence row and inferring the agent testing return could publish **mainRestartRecovery** and **recoveryCandidateEntry**. Public and internal session types were split, modern reads/writes gained runtime projection and preservation, and the internal candidate moved out of the published testing result.
7. **Handoff audit found the remaining compatibility seam.** Full entrypoint review showed that the deprecated whole-store **loadSessionStore/updateSessionStore** adapters still expose complete internal rows. This remains in scope because those APIs are shipped Plugin SDK contracts and whole-row writes can destroy the same recovery owner state this PR introduces.

Alternatives rejected:

- Process-local retry accounting: cannot survive the restart loop it is meant to stop.
- Deriving the durable budget from **restartRecoveryRuns**: conflates lifecycle fencing with product retry policy.
- Reusing the subagent rapid-time window: elapsed time and supervisor backoff do not demonstrate main-session health.
- Exposing the internal persistence row through any SDK entrypoint: turns recovery ownership into a public compatibility burden and lets whole-row writes destroy private state.
- Removing the deprecated compatibility or testing exports here: would break shipped SDK surfaces and exceed the recovery-specific scope.
- Replaying all 48 iterative commits onto new main without consolidation: repeatedly resurrects obsolete intermediate architectures and makes conflict resolution less reliable than applying the final reviewed tree.

## User Impact

A wedged main session can no longer trigger unbounded automatic resume across Gateway restarts. After three charged accepted or acceptance-uncertain attempts, OpenClaw quarantines the session before another automatic dispatch and asks the operator to inspect it and use **/new** or reset.

Healthy progress, replacement, or reset restores the full budget. Waiting alone does not. Existing plugin-visible session fields must remain available, while plugins must neither see nor accidentally overwrite the internal recovery state. The modern APIs satisfy that requirement at the current head; the deprecated whole-store compatibility APIs still require the fix documented above.

## Evidence

Previously reviewed range:

~~~text
base: 08843c74de0f632ef5b7808a9fcf9cb6c85ac967
head: 5d7c3d78e54e328aa5448ba2b1a4a8fdc49a1078
~~~

The previously verified merge result was **b0a38e374dcb5cb7566976560ad7182b49c81f49**, merging this head into **main@ffff72c43aedf5bdeb32a6836f577850207f8573**.

Proof valid for that exact old merge result:

- Focused recovery, compaction, and session proof: 230 tests passed on Docker Crabbox lease **cbx_c3e4e0c8917b**.
- Targeted lint and full **pnpm build** passed on Docker Crabbox lease **cbx_3a3579299845** (actual provider **local-container**, Docker runtime).
- Exact-head GitHub CI: all 15 workflows passed. The CI workflow completed with 50 successful jobs, 11 conditionally skipped jobs, and no failures: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29235146885
- The generated SDK type surface excluded **mainRestartRecovery** and **recoveryCandidateEntry**, with no recovery-internal checksum-only baseline update.
- Final default-Codex Auto Review completed with every accepted/actionable finding addressed for that head.
- Final ClawSweeper review found no contributor-facing blocker for that head.
- Real Telegram Desktop scenario proof remains available:
  - workflow: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28780448010
  - artifact: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28780448010/artifacts/8106022765
  - manifest: https://artifacts.openclaw.ai/mantis/telegram-desktop/pr-96230/run-28780448010-1/index.json

The Telegram baseline replayed the exhausted recovery turn before handling a fresh message. The candidate tombstoned the exhausted row and handled the fresh Telegram message without another automatic resume.

Current proof gaps:

- Deprecated **loadSessionStore/updateSessionStore** runtime projection and internal-state preservation are not implemented or tested.
- The PR is not rebased onto latest main and currently conflicts.
- No focused, changed-lane, build, Auto Review, exact-head CI, or exact-merge-result CI exists for the future rebased/fixed head.
